cp2: The geometry chain can still fail: a parcel with no baked envelope polygon, no situs address, and no live-parcel ring resolves to no centroid, and the contract makes geometry REQUIRED, so resolve() rejects and the card does not open. Today's code opens the card and leaves the map still. This is a deliberate behaviour trade named by invariant I5 and reported to the planner, not an oversight. The chain was widened (caller seed hint, baked polygon, authoritative placeKey, live ring, demoted address geocode) so the surface of that case is small.

Map clicks paint their card instantly and adopt the sealed sheet a moment later. Between those two moments the subject is the PREVIOUS parcel, so an export fired in that window is REFUSED with a target mismatch rather than run. Refusal is the correct failure, but it is a new user-visible state and the planner should know it exists.

Flood multiplicity is representable but NOT populated: the served tier2 facet is a scalar floodZone. The resolver widens it to a one-element set and stamps provenance.method 'single-zone-from-scalar' so the areaShare is never read as measured. The dispatch's item 9 cannot be fully satisfied client-side; it needs an engine-side multi-zone determination.

The InspectCard data-source swap was NOT done, on a source-grounded reason rather than time: the frozen contract cannot express what that card renders today. Provenance carries one source/sourceUrl and no atom DID list, so the AtomChip provenance popovers have no home; Setbacks has no per-axis governedBy or fieldNotes, so the setback X-ray disclosure has no home. Swapping the card onto the sheet as frozen would silently delete two shipped features. Reported, not worked around.

Compare's per-fact CELLS still read deriveBakedCardModel over a facets payload the compare tool fetches itself. Its headline now comes from the sealed sheet, and the R1-shaped adapter that fed the second composer is deleted, but the cell derivation is a remaining I2 gap. Named rather than hidden.

The US-only geocode filter drops features with NO countrycode, not only non-US ones. That exclusion set is stated in the module and covered by a test, per DEV_PROCESS ('an instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract'). If Photon ever omits countrycode for US addressable results this filter is too strict, and the single predicate isServedCountry is the one place to loosen it.
